title: Grateful Dead Live at Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke U on 1973-12-08
lineage: SBD:MR> C> DAT> CD> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture of a spiritually charged 1973 show with standout China‑Rider and an epic Other One, though the performance swings between inspired jams and some lackluster moments.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard mix that most listeners find clear, despite a slightly lower overall volume that may have been normalized. The concert delivers several high points—especially the loose China > Rider run, a fiery B.E. Woman, a long, exploratory Other One and an effective Outer Limits segment with Ned Lagin—but also drifts through weaker jams after He’s Gone, leaving some fans feeling the energy was uneven.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is mixed (average ~3.5) while recording quality is good (~4); weighting yields a combined rating around 3.6.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced soundboard recording; volume appears slightly lower than typical ’73 releases, possibly due to normalization. No major dropouts reported, though a filler segment from another date is present.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts subdued but builds with B.E. Woman, Big River and a hot China > Rider close; Disc Three shines with an extended Other One and spacey Outer Limits, while the early second‑set jam from He’s Gone feels less focused.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as meandering in the second set but praised for a strong delivery on 'B.E. Woman' and overall fire in the band.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ned Lagin’s synth contributions on the Outer Limits segment are noted as effective, though no specific comments about the main keyboardist.
